angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 27,956,009 km at 65.40 pc = 5.71 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: distance 65.402 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 65.402 +/- 0.785 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 15.5999 +/- 0.1074 mas (same row, RUWE 2.67), 145.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 40.184 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: radius 40.184 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 405.563 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.062) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 27,956,009 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4089 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: effective temperature 4089 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: effective temperature 4089 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Lep: spectral type K4III (1988MSS...C04....0H)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps Lep: projected rotation speed 2.45 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...704A..49B)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kiehling (1987), spectrophotometry of 60 bright F, G, K and M stars, 320-880 nm in 1 nm steps as normalised magnitudes) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.75 from 2024A&A...690A..97C; the 8 published values span log g 1.45 to 1.88, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...690A..97C)
